PR Summary by Qodo

Bind reason-5 merge decisions to the head named by their hold 🐞 Bug fix 🧪 Tests 📝 Documentation 🕐 40+ Minutes
AI Description

>
>• Require merge holds to name the PR head shown to the decision-maker.
>• Refuse reason-5 decisions after a history rewrite or non-review change; allow review-record-only
>  commits.
>• Document the new hold workflow and test gate and merge behavior offline.
>
Merge Risk 🟡 Medium

Blast radius 🟢 Low 💥 1 capability

- 1 affected end-to-end capability after fault-specific containment; implementation boundaries do not widen its functional scope. - The changed hold parsing, head comparison, gate verdict, and merge preflight all implement one bounded outcome: deciding whether an owner decision authorizes merging a sensitive-path PR. - The propagation path reaches the same gate and then the optional merge operation; these are not independent functional scopes. - The same end-to-end sensitive-path authorization behavior covers both the gate result and the merge preflight; a merge is a consumer of the authorization, not a separate functional scope.
Sources
[room.py\[2560-2586\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/d9722dd16c67573f47c9e7f8d2e9aaf5273d1576/room.py#L2560-L2586) ```python # the decision must answer this PR's hold: the lead's MERGE-HOLD-n (same n) for reason 5, these paths # and a head whose code is HEAD's but for review records, posted before it and not edited since (an # edit keeps the comment's id) n = a.decision.rsplit("-", 1)[1] holds = room.holds(f"MERGE-HOLD-{n}") lacking = [hold_problems(m["text"], a.pr, paths) for m in holds] whole = [h for h, problems in zip(holds, lacking) if not problems] moved = {h["id"]: hold_head_problem(root, h["text"], n, a.pr, head) for h in whole} fresh = [h for h in whole if not moved[h["id"]]] decisions = room.decisions(a.decision) pair = next(((h, d) for h in fresh for d in decisions if room.before(h, d)), None) if pair: g.ok("sensitive paths", f"{held}: allowed by {a.decision} (comment #{pair[1]['id']}), answering " f"MERGE-HOLD-{n} (comment #{pair[0]['id']})") return edited = next((h for h in fresh for d in decisions if h["id"] < d["id"]), None) hold = fresh[0] if fresh else None others = [h for h in whole if moved[h["id"]]] # a hold for other code: the one the decision answers, or the newest stale = next((h for h in others for d in decisions if room.before(h, d)), others[-1] if others else None) prefix = f"{held}; --allow-hold 5 --decision {a.decision}: " if edited: missing = f"MERGE-HOLD-{n} (comment #{edited['id']}) edited after {a.decision}: post a new hold" elif hold: missing = f"no trusted {a.decision} from the architect or Matthew after MERGE-HOLD-{n} (comment #{hold['id']})" elif stale: g.fail("sensitive paths", [(prefix + moved[stale["id"]], 5)]) return ```
Behavioral complexity 🟡 Medium 🧩 Interacting branches, Compatibility cases

- Before: a reason-5 decision was matched to a trusted hold by PR, reason, sensitive paths, comment order and edit status, without comparing the hold's code state. - After: the implementation parses a head token, resolves it as a commit, checks PR ancestry, diffs the hold head to the gated head, exempts only review-record paths, separates fresh from moved holds, and reports a stale-head refusal; gate and merge must both observe the same transition. - New correctness conditions: \(1\) old and current PR histories must be related correctly, including force-push cases; \(2\) review-record-only changes must remain allowable while any code or non-exempt path forces re-hold; \(3\) multiple holds with the same decision number must select only a current, unedited hold; and \(4\) merge must enforce exactly the same result as gate before its external effect. - These are newly interacting compatibility and ordering conditions, not complexity inherited merely from existing parsing or Git helpers.
Sources
[room.py\[2560-2586\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/d9722dd16c67573f47c9e7f8d2e9aaf5273d1576/room.py#L2560-L2586) ```python # the decision must answer this PR's hold: the lead's MERGE-HOLD-n (same n) for reason 5, these paths # and a head whose code is HEAD's but for review records, posted before it and not edited since (an # edit keeps the comment's id) n = a.decision.rsplit("-", 1)[1] holds = room.holds(f"MERGE-HOLD-{n}") lacking = [hold_problems(m["text"], a.pr, paths) for m in holds] whole = [h for h, problems in zip(holds, lacking) if not problems] moved = {h["id"]: hold_head_problem(root, h["text"], n, a.pr, head) for h in whole} fresh = [h for h in whole if not moved[h["id"]]] decisions = room.decisions(a.decision) pair = next(((h, d) for h in fresh for d in decisions if room.before(h, d)), None) if pair: g.ok("sensitive paths", f"{held}: allowed by {a.decision} (comment #{pair[1]['id']}), answering " f"MERGE-HOLD-{n} (comment #{pair[0]['id']})") return edited = next((h for h in fresh for d in decisions if h["id"] < d["id"]), None) hold = fresh[0] if fresh else None others = [h for h in whole if moved[h["id"]]] # a hold for other code: the one the decision answers, or the newest stale = next((h for h in others for d in decisions if room.before(h, d)), others[-1] if others else None) prefix = f"{held}; --allow-hold 5 --decision {a.decision}: " if edited: missing = f"MERGE-HOLD-{n} (comment #{edited['id']}) edited after {a.decision}: post a new hold" elif hold: missing = f"no trusted {a.decision} from the architect or Matthew after MERGE-HOLD-{n} (comment #{hold['id']})" elif stale: g.fail("sensitive paths", [(prefix + moved[stale["id"]], 5)]) return ```
Potential damage 🔴 High 🩹 Integrity

- If the new validation incorrectly accepts a stale hold, cmd_merge can proceed with a GitHub merge for code that the decision did not cover. - The resulting merge is an external repository change and may require a deliberate revert or corrective PR plus a fresh review; reverting room.py afterward does not undo an already completed merge. - This is a bounded integrity risk for the sensitive-path merge authorization capability, not a claim that unrelated application data is corrupted. - Potentially recoverable only through explicit repository remediation: revert or corrective PR, review, and a new merge decision. - Code rollback prevents recurrence but does not compensate for an already merged change.
Sources
[room.py\[2560-2586\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/d9722dd16c67573f47c9e7f8d2e9aaf5273d1576/room.py#L2560-L2586) ```python # the decision must answer this PR's hold: the lead's MERGE-HOLD-n (same n) for reason 5, these paths # and a head whose code is HEAD's but for review records, posted before it and not edited since (an # edit keeps the comment's id) n = a.decision.rsplit("-", 1)[1] holds = room.holds(f"MERGE-HOLD-{n}") lacking = [hold_problems(m["text"], a.pr, paths) for m in holds] whole = [h for h, problems in zip(holds, lacking) if not problems] moved = {h["id"]: hold_head_problem(root, h["text"], n, a.pr, head) for h in whole} fresh = [h for h in whole if not moved[h["id"]]] decisions = room.decisions(a.decision) pair = next(((h, d) for h in fresh for d in decisions if room.before(h, d)), None) if pair: g.ok("sensitive paths", f"{held}: allowed by {a.decision} (comment #{pair[1]['id']}), answering " f"MERGE-HOLD-{n} (comment #{pair[0]['id']})") return edited = next((h for h in fresh for d in decisions if h["id"] < d["id"]), None) hold = fresh[0] if fresh else None others = [h for h in whole if moved[h["id"]]] # a hold for other code: the one the decision answers, or the newest stale = next((h for h in others for d in decisions if room.before(h, d)), others[-1] if others else None) prefix = f"{held}; --allow-hold 5 --decision {a.decision}: " if edited: missing = f"MERGE-HOLD-{n} (comment #{edited['id']}) edited after {a.decision}: post a new hold" elif hold: missing = f"no trusted {a.decision} from the architect or Matthew after MERGE-HOLD-{n} (comment #{hold['id']})" elif stale: g.fail("sensitive paths", [(prefix + moved[stale["id"]], 5)]) return ```
Assessed commit d9722dd
Diagram

```mermaid graph TD L["Lead"] --> H["Head-named hold"] --> G["Gate or merge"] --> V{"Valid head history?"} -->|Yes| R{"Review-only changes?"} -->|Yes| M["Merge allowed"] D["Owner decision"] --> G V -->|No| N["New hold required"] R -->|No| N ```
High-Level Assessment

>The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Require an exact head match
- ➕ Simpler validation without an ancestry or changed-path check. - ➖ Review-record commits, including decision bookkeeping, would require another hold and decision.
>**Recommendation:** Keep the ancestry-and-review-exemption approach. It prevents a decision from authorizing newly changed code while allowing the existing review-record workflow to advance the PR head.

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
